items.title: Adopted retarded solution selection: the physical branch carries no incoming free field
items.statement: Adopt as a physical assumption of this framework the following solution-selection rule for the classical vacuum model on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the constants and SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] (so $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$). (a) [Formulation] In the potential formulation of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] with the conventions of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], for a $C^2$ potential pair in Lorenz gauge the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] is equivalent to the decoupled sourced wave equations $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$. The wave expression $W$ is invariant under $t\mapsto-t$; where explicit retarded or advanced constructions for a prescribed history exist, they give distinguished particular solutions built from the corresponding forward or backward fundamental kernels. Every other solution differs from a chosen particular solution by a source-free addition; retarded and advanced particular solutions also differ by such an addition. This describes the affine free-solution freedom, not a claim that arbitrary histories have exactly two solutions or that either construction always exists. (b) [Adopted rule] The framework adopts the retarded branch with no free field added: the physical potential pair of the model is the retarded one, that is, the one whose support and propagation lie in the forward light cones of the source and which carries no field arriving from the past independently of the source. For the zero-incoming model the selected sourced solution has no independently prescribed homogeneous addition. If nonzero Cauchy data are instead prescribed, their compatible homogeneous addition is a separate initial-data model; it is not equivalent to setting every free addition to zero. The advanced construction and independent incoming free fields are excluded by the present retarded selection. (c) [Status and scope] This is an adopted extra temporal condition carrying the model's arrow-of-time content. It is not a theorem, not a consequence of the time-symmetric wave or Maxwell equations (which admit advanced and free solutions as mathematical objects), and not a deduction from experiment; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity, support or decay for any source class, all of which must be supplied separately by theorems of this page. It selects a solution only of the models to which it is applied; it introduces no product of distributions, no source model, no self-force, no radiation reaction, no measured signal and no statistical claim. The retarded compact-source branch to which this selection applies is developed on this page as a conditional theorem, and the point-source branch is developed later on this page; neither existence statement is part of this postulate. For the separately declared point-source branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as in its exact source/field interfaces, and adopt the same no-free-addition retarded selection in the weak equations of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], for the locally integrable field and proper point-current types of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. This extends the selection's model scope explicitly; neither existence nor an arbitrary convolution of noncompact distributions is postulated.
items.strategy: A postulate: the item records an adopted solution-selection rule, and receives a source/scope review rather than a proof. The review checks that (i) the formulation correctly displays the wave expression $W$, its time-reversal symmetry, the retarded and advanced fundamental-solution branches and the free-field freedom, all with the exact interfaces of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] and [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; (ii) the adopted rule is stated as a modelling choice with its arrow-of-time content, and is not presented as a consequence of the equations; (iii) the formulation does not pretend to prove existence or uniqueness for any source class and expressly defers those to the consuming theorems; (iv) no empirical, statistical, measurement or apparatus claim is made, and no quantitative precision is invented; and (v) the scope exclusions (advanced branch, free fields, arbitrary distributions, self-force) are explicit. The classical textbook treatments listed in the sources present the retarded/advanced distinction and the extra choice of the retarded Green function (Tong's 'extra choice' at the displayed page); they support the formulation and the honest status, and are not evidence for the physical correctness of the choice. The weak point-source extension is an explicit physical selection on the already-adopted singular-source equations, not a deduction from the old smooth-only potential theorem. A consuming mathematical theorem must construct its actual history integrals and prove weak admissibility.
items.physical_scope: Adopted selection rule for the classical vacuum Maxwell/wave model in the framework's inertial laboratory chart and SI conventions: the physical potential pair is the retarded one with zero incoming free field, both for the smooth compact-source branch and for the separately declared weak point-source equations. Excluded: existence, uniqueness, regularity or decay claims for any source class (consuming theorems must supply them); empirical, statistical or measurement claims; the advanced branch and free fields as physical solutions; products of distributions, self-force, radiation reaction and any apparatus model.

items.title: Uniformly subluminal prescribed worldline, retarded root and retarded geometric data off the worldline
items.statement: Let the laboratory region, inertial chart, spatial Euclidean structure and SI units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], in particular $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. A **retarded point-geometry datum** consists of a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs ([[def-em-sources]](a)) and a prescribed map $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^3$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) together with a constant $0\le v_*<c$ such that $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); the spacetime curve $s\mapsto(z(s),s)$ is the laboratory reading of a prescribed massive future timelike worldline of the physical model ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]), and $v_*$ is a declared bound on its coordinate speed, not a measured quantity. Write $\Gamma:=\{(z(s),s):s\in\mathbb R\}$ and $D:=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R:x\ne z(t)\}$ for the open off-worldline observation domain. Then: (a) [Retarded root] For every observation event $(x,t)\in D$ there is exactly one $s=s(x,t)<t$ with $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$; the map $s:D\to\mathbb R$ is of class $C^3$, and with the data of (b) below one has $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$ and $\nabla_xs=-n/(c\kappa)$ ([[lem-em-global-retarded-root]], whose $C^3$ branch applies because $z$ is $C^3$ and uniformly subluminal). (b) [Retarded data] For $(x,t)\in D$ define $R:=x-z(s(x,t))$, $r:=|R|>0$, $n:=R/r$, $\beta:=z'(s(x,t))/c$, $\kappa:=1-n\cdot\beta$, $\dot\beta:=z''(s(x,t))/c$; then $r=c(t-s)$ and $\kappa\in[1-v_*/c,\,1+v_*/c]\subseteq(0,\infty)$. On $D$ the objects $r$ and $n$ are of class $C^3$, $\beta$ and $\kappa$ are of class $C^2$, and $\dot\beta$ is of class $C^1$ (each is a composition of the $C^3$ root with $z$ or its derivatives). (c) [Emission-event data and emitted spheres] At an emission event $s_0\in\mathbb R$ and a direction $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$ for $r>0$, and $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\kappa_0:=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Then $(x_r,t_r)\in D$ and $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$ for every $r>0$: the sphere $\{x_r\}$ at observation time $t_r$ is emitted at the single event $s_0$. (d) [Branches and scope] Only the all-time uniformly subluminal branch (a)-(c) is defined by this datum. For a curve prescribed on a finite interval $J$ the same formulas define retarded data only at observation events for which the root equation has a solution $s\in J$; each consumer must assume that cone intersection explicitly. Pointwise subluminality $|z'(s)|<c$ for every finite $s$ does not imply (a): the companion example on the examples page exhibits a smooth curve with $|z'|<c$ pointwise for which the retarded equation has no root at some event, so the uniform bound $v_*<c$, or an explicit cone-intersection hypothesis, is part of the datum. This definition is kinematic: it fixes the root, the retarded data and the notation, and asserts no field, no dynamics, no force law, no self-force and no empirical content. The identification of these data with the emission data of the physical field is made by the selection postulate [[post-em-radiation-selection]] together with the theorems of this page.
items.strategy: An explicit definition with its well-definedness discharged by a cited mathematical supplier. Existence, uniqueness and $C^3$ regularity of $s$ on $D$, together with $\kappa\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$ and the derivative formulas, are exactly the all-time uniformly subluminal $C^3$ branch of [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] (its statement covers every event of $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, hence every off-worldline event, and identifies equality $s=t$ with $x=z(t)$); no new analysis is needed, and the phrase 'prescribed worldline' is licensed by [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]](a),(c), which relates chart readings $t\mapsto r(t)$ of massive worldlines to the condition $|r'(t)|<c$. Clause (c) is the elementary root check $t_r-s_0=|x_r-z(s_0)|/c=r/c$ combined with the uniqueness in (a); no boundedness of $z''$ is used. Clause (d) records the branch boundaries honestly: the finite-history and nonuniform cases are left to consumers, and the failure of existence under mere pointwise subluminality is not asserted here but exhibited on the examples page. The definition introduces no physical field, so no Maxwell, self-force or empirical assertion is made; the cross-reference to the selection postulate records that the retarded root is the kinematic object that the adopted selection turns into an emission time. No choice principle beyond that carried by the cited root lemma is used.
items.physical_scope: Kinematic definition of the retarded emission data of a prescribed uniformly subluminal $C^3$ worldline in the framework's laboratory chart: retarded root, distance, direction, speed ratio, emission-time Jacobian and emitted-sphere family off the worldline. Excluded: any field, Maxwell equation, dynamics, force law, self-force, radiation reaction, existence under a merely pointwise subluminal or finite-history curve, and every empirical or measurement claim.

items.title: Zonal and quadratic sphere moments for the polar surface measure on $S^2$
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the dipole and emitted-power items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-36.notes.md)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), let $e_3:=(0,0,1)$ and write $n_3=n\cdot e_3$ for $n\in S^2$. Then: (a) [Zonal identity] for every continuous $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$, $$\int_{S^2}f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du.$$ (b) [Linear weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)\,f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3\int_{-1}^{1}u\,f(u)\,du.$$ (c) [Quadratic weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3^{2}\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}f(u)\,du+\pi\,(a_1^{2}+a_2^{2})\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})f(u)\,du.$$ (d) [Moments] $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$ $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=\frac{4\pi}{3}|a|^2,\qquad \int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^2,$$ where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker symbol and $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) [Scope] (a)-(d) are identities for the polar surface measure of the unit sphere with only the stated continuity of $f$; they assert no physical field, flux or radiation statement. The measure is finite, so all displayed integrals are absolutely convergent; $f$ need not be nonnegative. For the uses on this page $f$ is a rational function with denominator bounded below by $1-b>0$, hence continuous on $[-1,1]$.
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Parametrize $S^2$ by $X(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$. Computing the coordinate cross product with the sin/cos derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) gives $X_\theta\times X_\varphi=\sin\theta\,X(\theta,\varphi)$, whose norm is $\sin\theta\ge0$; by [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]] and [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]] the chart surface integral of $F(n)=f(n_3)$ is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$, with the seam and the poles lying on the parameter boundary exactly as in the sphere-area computation, so this is the integral over $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-parameter-boundary-exceptions-do-not-affect-surface-integrals|the boundary-exception convention]]). The chart measure equals the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). By [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]] the $\varphi$-integral is the constant $2\pi$, and with $P(u):=\int_0^u f$ ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]) the chain rule and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta=[-P(\cos\theta)]_0^{\pi}=P(1)-P(-1)=\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du$, using $\cos0=1$, $\cos\pi=-1$ and the derivative $\cos'=-\sin$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]). This proves (a), including the endpoint values by continuity of $P\circ\cos$ on $[0,\pi]$ and the two-sided fundamental theorem. (b) Write $n\cdot a=a_1n_1+a_2n_2+a_3n_3$. The maps $\eta_1(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(-n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and $\eta_2(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(n_1,-n_2,n_3)$ are orthogonal and preserve $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); since $n_1f(n_3)$ and $n_2f(n_3)$ change sign under $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ respectively, the substitution formula for the measure-preserving involution $\eta_i$ (indicators by definition, simple functions by linearity, bounded Borel functions by the usual approximation, exactly as in the vanishing-first-moment computation of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]) gives $\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=-\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=0$ for $i=1,2$; the remaining term is $a_3\int n_3f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi a_3\int_{-1}^1uf(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=uf(u)$. (c) Expanding the square, the mixed terms $n_in_jf(n_3)$ with $i\ne j$ vanish by the same reflection argument; the terms $n_1^2$ and $n_2^2$ are equal by the swap $(n_1,n_2,n_3)\mapsto(n_2,n_1,n_3)$, which is orthogonal and preserves $\sigma$. Hence $\int n_1^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\int n_2^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\tfrac12\int(1-n_3^2)f(n_3)d\sigma=\pi\int_{-1}^1(1-u^2)f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=(1-u^2)f(u)$, while $\int n_3^2f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^1u^2f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=u^2f(u)$; linearity of the $\sigma$-integral on the (finite-measure) integrable functions is [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]. This proves (c). (d) Taking $f=1$ in (a) gives $\sigma(S^2)=2\pi\cdot2=4\pi$, which also evaluates the closed form of [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]] at $n=3$ together with the Gamma values $\Gamma(5/2)=(3/2)(1/2)\Gamma(1/2)=3\sqrt\pi/4$ ([[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]]), so the two routes agree. Taking $f=1$ in (b),(c) gives $\int n_if(n_3)=0$ for $i=1,2$ and the matrix identity $\int n_in_jd\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$ (equivalently $\int(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$); the first moment statement is the three-dimensional case of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]. Finally $|n\times a|^2=|a|^2-(n\cdot a)^2$ by the cross-product norm identity ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), so $\int|n\times a|^2d\sigma=4\pi|a|^2-(4\pi/3)|a|^2=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$. Clause (e) records that no physical interpretation is attached. No choice principle beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ (carried by the surface-measure interface) is used.

items.title: Retarded potentials, Lorenz gauge and Maxwell fields of a compactly supported conserved smooth source
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the retarded-kernel and Cauchy suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], so that $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is the wave expression of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. Let $a>0$, $t_0<T$ and let $ho:\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R	o\mathbb R$, $J:\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R	o\mathbb R^3$ be source fields of [[def-em-sources]] that are jointly of class $C^\infty$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], vanish identically outside the compact set $\overline B_a(0)	imes[t_0,T]$, and satisfy the continuity equation $\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ everywhere --- the compatibility condition that [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] shows to be forced by the Maxwell system, here assumed for the prescribed source. Define the retarded potentials by the explicit retarded integrals $$\varphi(x,t):= rac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3} rac{ho igl(y,t-|x-y|/c igr)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad A(x,t):= rac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3} rac{J igl(y,t-|x-y|/c igr)}{|x-y|}\,dy,$$ and put $E:=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=
abla	imes A$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then: (a) [Smoothness and wave equations] $\varphi$ and each component of $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$, and $W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$ pointwise. (b) [Lorenz gauge] With $G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$ one has $G=0$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$: the retarded pair is in Lorenz gauge, the continuity hypothesis supplies this identity and the total-charge conclusion (f). (c) [Maxwell fields] $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ and the tuple $(E,B,ho,J)$ satisfies the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the whole of $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$: $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $
abla	imes E=-\partial_tB$, $
abla	imes B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. (d) [No field before the source] $E=B=0$ at every event with $t<t_0$ (indeed $\varphi=A=0$ there): the selected retarded solution carries no field from before the source acted. (e) [Zero-data Cauchy identification] For every $t_1<t_0$ the pair $(\varphi,A)$ restricted to $\mathbb R^3	imes[t_1,\infty)$ is the unique $C^2$ extension solution of the wave Cauchy problem of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] at time $t_1$ with zero Cauchy data and sources $ho/\varepsilon_0$, $\mu_0J$. (f) [Total charge] The total charge $Q(t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}ho(y,t)\,dy$ is zero for every $t$: a source that is smooth, compactly supported in space and restricted to a compact time interval and satisfies continuity carries zero total charge, so this branch does not model an eternal isolated nonzero charge. (g) [Scope] This is the compact smooth branch with an adopted causal selection; it asserts nothing about point, line or sheet sources, about weak or distributional branches, about finite-energy or decay properties, about radiation reaction or self-force, and no empirical claim. In particular the fields of a prescribed isolated point charge with an eternal worldline are not covered by this theorem and are supplied separately by the point-source items of this page.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) $ho,J$ are $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R)$; clause (b) of [[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]] applied to $h=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and componentwise to $h=\mu_0J_k$ states that $(K*h)(x,t)=\int h(y,t-|x-y|/c)/(4\pi|x-y|)dy$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$ and satisfies $W(K*h)=h$ pointwise, which is exactly the display. Note the identification $\varphi=\varepsilon_0^{-1}K*ho$, $A=\mu_0K*J$ is the framework's form of the adopted retarded selection of [[post-em-radiation-selection]]; the selected branch is the object being computed, not assumed to exist a priori. (b) Differentiate the explicit retarded integral. In the substitution $y'=x-y$, which leaves the integral unchanged by translation invariance of Lebesgue measure ([[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]), the kernel $1/(4\pi|y'|)$ is independent of $x$, so differentiating under the integral sign in $x$ (direct dominated difference quotients: on each compact (x,t) parameter neighborhood all derivatives of h(x-y',t-|y'|/c) vanish outside one bounded y'-ball and are bounded by their appropriate derivative suprema; each quotient is dominated by that constant times |y'|^-1, integrable by [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], so [[thm-dominated-convergence]] gives each derivative identity. The smooth nonsingular [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] is used separately for the charge integral, not at this pole) gives $\partial_{x^i}(K*h)=K*(\partial_{y^i}h)$; differentiating in $t$ gives $\partial_t(K*h)=K*(\partial_th)$. Therefore $\operatorname{div}A=\mu_0K*(\operatorname{div}J)$ and $c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}K*(\partial_tho)=\mu_0K*(\partial_tho)$ because $c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0\cdot\varepsilon_0^{-1}c^{-2}$ reduces to $\mu_0$ (equivalently $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$, [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Adding, $G=\mu_0K*(\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J)=0$ by the assumed continuity. (c) $\varphi,A$ are $C^\infty$, hence $C^2$, and clause (a) of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] (instantiated at $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$) states the exact identities $\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG$ and $
abla	imes B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+
abla G$; with (a) and (b) these read $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $
abla	imes B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J$. The two source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $
abla	imes E+\partial_tB=0$ are automatic for a potential pair by the curl-divergence and curl-gradient cancellation recorded in clause (c) of the same item and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. This is the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. items.title: Controlled electric-dipole far field and retarded-time radiated power of a compact smooth source
items.statement: Assume the setting and hypotheses of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by its suppliers: $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $a>0$, $t_0<T$, jointly $C^\infty$ fields $\rho,J$ vanishing outside $\overline B_a(0)\times[t_0,T]$ and satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$; let $\varphi,A$ be the retarded potentials and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ the fields, with $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Adopt the causal selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]]: these retarded fields are the fields of the source model (the compact smooth instance established by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]). Define the **time-dependent electric dipole moment** $$p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\,\rho(y,u)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3$$ (componentwise, about the fixed chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; it is the fixed-time analogue of the static source moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]]), and, as in the asymptotic theorem, $I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$, $V(n,u):=\partial_uI(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$ and $$D(u):=\frac{a}{c}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|\,dy.$$ Then: (a) [Moment identities] $p\in C^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$, $p'(u)=\int_{B_a}J(y,u)\,dy$, $p''(u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u)\,dy$, $\int_{B_a}\rho_t(y,u)\,dy=0$ and the total charge $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)\,dy$ vanishes for every $u$. (b) [Dipole replacement error] $|V(n,u)-p''(u)|\le D(u)$ for every $n\in S^2$ and every $u\in[t_0,T]$: the explicit absolute error of the dipole approximation to the source's transverse current moment. (c) [Leading fields] With $\Gamma_E$, $\Gamma_B$ the constants of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](b) (depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the listed source suprema), for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$, $r\ge2a$: $$\Bigl|E\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p''(u))\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r},\qquad \Bigl|B\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{n\times E(rn,u+\tfrac rc)}{c}\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}.$$ The displayed dipole field approximates the actual leading far field $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$ with the stated absolute $D(u)/r$ error. Equality of these leading fields requires $n\times(n\times(V-p''))=0$; $V=p''$ and, in particular, $D(u)=0$ are sufficient. All errors are uniform in $n$ at fixed $u$. (d) [Retarded-time radiated power] The limit of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](c) equals $\mu_0|p''(u)|^2/(6\pi c)+R(u)$ with the explicit absolute error $$|R(u)|\le\frac{\mu_0\bigl(2|p''(u)|D(u)+D(u)^2\bigr)}{4\pi c},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\ \text{ whenever } D(u)=0.$$ The evaluation uses the sphere moment $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$ of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d). The limit is at fixed retarded time $u$, not at fixed observation time. (e) [Scope] The compact smooth source branch only; the dipole error is absolute and explicitly controlled by $D(u)$, and no assertion is made that slow or 'nonrelativistic' source motion alone makes $D(u)$ small -- that is a hypothesis on the source's time variation. No point charge, no moving point source, no radiation reaction, no self-force and no empirical or measurement content; the failure of the correspondence with an oscillator for rapidly varying sources is retained through $D(u)$. Separately retain the sharper actual source estimate $|B(rn,u+r/c)-n\times E_{\rm lead}(n,u,r)/c|\le\Gamma_B/r^2$, with $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$; the bound against the actual E uses the combined constant displayed in (c).
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]]. (a) $\rho$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, so $u\mapsto p(u)$ is $C^\infty$ by differentiation under the integral sign ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]) and $p'(u)=\int y\,\rho_t(y,u)dy$; integrating by parts componentwise over a ball containing the support via the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], boundary term zero by compact support) gives $\int y_i\partial_t\rho\,dy=-\int y_i\operatorname{div}J\,dy=\int J_i\,dy$, since $\partial_i(y_iJ_k)$ contributes $J_i$ and the remaining divergence term integrates to zero. Replacing $J$ by $J_t$ (equivalently differentiating in $u$ under the integral sign) gives $p''=\int J_t$. The vanishing $\int\rho_t=0$ is the same divergence theorem with weight $1$ (equivalently clause (f) of [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]), and the total charge vanishes because $\rho$ is supported in $t\in[t_0,T]$. (b) For fixed $y\in B_a$ the one-variable function $v\mapsto J_t(y,v)$ is $C^1$ on the interval between $u$ and $u+n\cdot y/c$, whose length is at most $a/c$; for nonzero vector difference w choose its fixed unit direction e=w/|w| and apply the scalar mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]) to e dot J_t; finite Euclidean Cauchy-Schwarz bounds |e dot J_tt| by |J_tt| (the zero difference is immediate), giving $|J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)-J_t(y,u)|\le(a/c)\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|$ componentwise, and integrating over $B_a$ with the integral triangle inequality and monotonicity ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) gives (b). (c) Clause (b) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] writes $E(rn,u+r/c)=E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)+$ remainder with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times V(n,u))/(4\pi r)$ and remainder $O(r^{-2})$ bounded by $\Gamma_E r^{-2}$. Substituting $V=p''+(V-p'')$ and using $|n\times(n\times w)|\le|w|$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]) gives the first bound; The supplier bounds B-n cross E_lead/c by Gamma_B/r² and E-E_lead by Gamma_E/r²; the triangle inequality therefore gives the displayed (Gamma_B+Gamma_E/c)/r² bound against the actual E. D=0 suffices for exact dipole power; no converse is inferred from an error bound. (d) By clause (c) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] the limit equals $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\int_{S^2}|n\times V|^2d\sigma$. Replacing $V$ by $p''$ changes the integrand by at most $(2|p''|D+D^2)$ pointwise (expand $|n\times V|^2-|n\times p''|^2$ and use the bound (b), the linearity of the cross product and the integral triangle inequality), so the integral changes by at most $4\pi(2|p''|D+D^2)$ and the limit by $\mu_0(2|p''|D+D^2)/(4\pi c)$. The exact dipole value uses $|n\times p''|^2=|p''|^2-(n\cdot p'')^2$ and clause (d) of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]]: $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=4\pi|p''|^2-(4\pi/3)|p''|^2=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$, and $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\cdot(8\pi/3)=\mu_0/(6\pi c)$. (e) records that the error coefficient $D(u)$ constrains the source's own time variation and that the limit is a fixed-retarded-time limit, as in the supplier; no self-force, point-source, decay or empirical claim is added.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the point-source change-of-variables suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]] ($c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$), let $q\in\mathbb R$ and let $z$, $v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline of a point charge, [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the constant $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), write $\Omega:=\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$ and $\Gamma:=\{(z(s),s):s\in\mathbb R\}$, and let $ho,J$ be the point-source distributions of that charge on the worldline in the declared point-source class of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) (the $C^3$ branch of the point-current construction). Let $(\varphi,A)$ be the retarded history pairings of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]](b) -- the framework's retarded construction for this source under the adopted selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]] -- and define $E:=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=
abla	imes A$ on the off-worldline domain $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then: (a) [Potentials] $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A= eta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, where $r,\kappa, eta$ are the retarded data of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](b); the zero extensions of $\varphi,A$ to $\Gamma$ are locally integrable on $\Omega$. (b) [Exact fields] On $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $$E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}},\qquad E_{\mathrm{vel}}= rac{C(1-| eta|^2)(n- eta)}{\kappa^3r^2},\qquad E_{\mathrm{acc}}= rac{C\,n	imes igl((n- eta)	imes\dot eta igr)}{c\,\kappa^3r},\qquad B= rac{n	imes E}{c},$$ and $E,B$ are of class $C^1$ there; the velocity part obeys $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$. (c) [Uniform far-zone remainder] For every emission event $s_0$ and direction $n\in S^2$, with $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $ eta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\dot eta_0:=z''(s_0)/c$ and $\kappa_0:=1-n\cdot eta_0$: $(x_r,t_r)\in\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, and $$E(x_r,t_r)= rac{C\,n	imes igl((n- eta_0)	imes\dot eta_0 igr)}{c\,\kappa_0^3\,r}+ho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|ho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C| rac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}\,r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)= rac{n	imes E(x_r,t_r)}{c};$$ the bound is uniform in $n$ at fixed $s_0$. (d) [Scope] These are the stipulated retarded model fields of the prescribed charge: the item identifies, through the same adopted causal selection used by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] for the compact branch, the point-source potentials and fields of the model, and proves their exact form and bounds. It asserts no value of the fields on the worldline $\Gamma$ (where the formulas are undefined and the self-field is singular), no integral or energy statement, no self-force and no radiation reaction, and derives no mass. The uniform bound $v_*<c$ and the exclusion of $\Gamma$ are essential hypotheses; the companion example page shows that a merely pointwise subluminal curve can fail to have a retarded root, and no uniformity in the emission event $s_0$ is claimed ($z''$ is not assumed bounded). The signed constant $C$ is retained in every displayed formula while absolute-value bounds use $|C|$. (e) [Constructed weak solution] Let $\Phi,\Upsilon$ be the global regular potential distributions in (a), and let $\mathcal E=-
abla\Phi-\partial_t\Upsilon$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{curl}\Upsilon$. By [[thm-em-retarded-point-distributional-maxwell]], their representatives are exactly the locally integrable zero extensions of the displayed off-worldline fields. They satisfy all four identities of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with the proper all-time point pair $ho,J$; the volume source parts are zero. Thus they are an admitted point-source model of the explicit physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], under the same retarded selection. The potentials satisfy $W\Phi=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $W\Upsilon=\mu_0J$ and the distributional Lorenz identity. This existence and solution property is supplied by the mathematical theorem, not by the selection postulate or by the compact-source theorem. The zero extensions on the null graph give no physically defined self-field and no nonlinear products there. All original exact field, regularity and uniform far-zone branches remain as stated. On each product neighborhood disjoint from $\Gamma$ the fields satisfy the smooth source-free Maxwell equations. Consequently any use of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] by the radiation items is local on such neighborhoods, with $ho=J=0$; it neither applies that smooth theorem across the point source nor forms self-work or a global finite-energy identity.

items.reference: completed-expansion-arguments.md#R3; general weighted angular computation from R4 proved here using earlier suppliers
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $z,v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline, $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), let $s_0$ be an emission event with $z'(s_0)=0$ (the charge is momentarily at rest in the laboratory chart), and put $a:=z''(s_0)$ and, for $n\in S^2$, $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields of the charge given by [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and $S:=E	imes B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Then: (a) [Field on the emitted sphere] For every $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$, $$E(x_r,t_r)= rac{C\,n	imes(n	imes a)}{c^2r}+ho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|ho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C| rac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)= rac{n	imes E(x_r,t_r)}{c}.$$ (b) [Angular flux density] The limits $$ rac{dP}{d\sigma}(n):=\lim_{r	o\infty}r^2\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)= rac{C^{2}\,|n	imes(n	imes a)|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}},\qquad P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\int_{S^2} rac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)\,d\sigma(n),$$ exist with the convergence uniform in $n\in S^2$; $d\sigma$ is the polar surface measure of the unit sphere (equal to the chart surface measure by [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). (c) [Total power] $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)= rac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\cdot rac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}= rac{q^2|a|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ the Larmor power of the momentarily resting prescribed charge. (d) [Angular distribution] For $a
e0$, define $	heta\in[0,\pi]$ by $\cos	heta=(n\cdot a)/|a|$; this angle exists uniquely because the quotient is in $[-1,1]$ and cosine is continuous and strictly decreasing from $1$ to $-1$ on $[0,\pi]$. When $a=0$ the angle is undefined and $dP/d\sigma\equiv0$. Then $$ rac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)= rac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\sin^2	heta:$$ when $q
e0$ and $a
e0$ the radiation pattern vanishes exactly along the instantaneous acceleration axis and is maximal in the perpendicular plane; when $q=0$ it vanishes in every direction; $\int_{S^2}dP/d\sigma\,d\sigma=P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$. If $a=0$ all displayed radiation quantities vanish. (e) [Scope and conventions] The result is exact at an emission event at which the charge is instantaneously at rest in the laboratory chart: then $\kappa_0(n)=1$ for every $n$, so no retarded-time conversion factor appears and the displayed limits are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time. The item uses only the prescribed worldline and the retarded model fields -- it is not a mechanical evolution law, does not assert a self-force or radiation reaction, derives no mass, and makes no empirical or measurement claim. For a general emission event the exact formula and its low-speed comparison are supplied by clause (f); 'slow' motion alone is never substituted for an error bound. The prescribed curve, the uniform subluminal bound and $z'(s_0)=0$ are hypotheses; for a varying-velocity worldline the instantaneous rest event is a single parameter value, not an interval. (f) [General low-speed branch] At any emission event, without imposing $z'(s_0)=0$ for this clause, define emitted power by the weighted far-zone flux integral $\kappa_0(n)\,r^2\,n\cdot S$ on the emitted spheres, with $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot eta_0$, $ eta_0=z'(s_0)/c$, $| eta_0|\le v_*/c$ and $\gamma_0:=(1-| eta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$. items.title: Relativistic emitted power of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the setting be that of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: a charge $q\in\mathbb R$ ($C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$) on a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline $z$ in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], with retarded fields $E,B$ off the worldline and the uniform far-zone remainder of that item; let $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]). Let $s_0$ be an emission event, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\gamma_0:=(1-|\beta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$, $a:=z''(s_0)$, and for $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\kappa_0(n):=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Define the **emitted power at the emission event $s_0$** by the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}\kappa_0(n)\,r^{2}\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)\,d\sigma(n),$$ $d\sigma$ the polar surface measure (equal to the chart surface measure). The weight $\kappa_0$ is the emission-time/observation-time conversion factor of the retarded root, $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$, equivalently the moving-boundary correction $S\cdot n-(z'\cdot n)u$ at leading radiation order, where $u=|S|/c$ for the transverse far field. Then: (a) [Weighted flux limit] The limit exists and $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}\frac{\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}}{\kappa_0(n)^{5}}\,d\sigma(n).$$ (b) [Closed form and four-acceleration form] If $b:=|\beta_0|<1$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp$ is decomposed along $\beta_0=|\beta_0|e_3$ and perpendicular to it, then $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{q^{2}\gamma_0^{6}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)=\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\,\eta(A,A),$$ where $A$ is the four-acceleration of the worldline at $s_0$ and $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](e)). At $\beta_0=0$ the weight is $1$ and (b) reduces to the instantaneous-rest Larmor power of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) [Low-speed comparison] For every $\delta\in(0,1)$ and every emission event with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$, $$\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)\le\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \Bigl|P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)-\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\Bigr|\le\frac{3\delta^{2}}{(1-\delta^{2})^{3}}\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ a comparison uniform over the events with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. In particular the instantaneous-rest formula is the exact $\delta=0$ case, and no term of the comparison is asserted to be small without the explicit hypothesis $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. (d) [Scope] $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ is the power emitted at the single retarded event $s_0$ per unit emission time, defined by the weighted far-zone flux; it is not a coordinate-time loss rate of a dynamical particle, and no dynamics (self-force, radiation reaction, mass), no uniformity in $s_0$, and no empirical or measurement claim is made. The near fields are $O(r^{-2})$ with their uniform remainder as in [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]](c), so their contribution to the weighted $r^2$ flux vanishes; the $\kappa_0$-weighting is part of the definition of emitted power and is not an additional physical assumption.
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) On the emitted sphere the retarded data are those of the emission event ($s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]](d)), and the uniform remainder gives $E= E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}+\rho_E$ with $E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)/(c\kappa_0^{3}r)$, $|\rho_E|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ and $B=n\times E/c$. For such fields $n\cdot S=|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)$ (expand $E\times(n\times E/c)$ and use the triple-product orthogonality, [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Therefore $\kappa_0r^{2}n\cdot S=\kappa_0r^{2}|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)=\kappa_0|C|^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{6})+O(r^{-1})$ with a remainder controlled by the uniform bound ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); note $C^{2}=|C|^{2}$ as squares. Integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) gives (a) with $\dot\beta_0=a/c$ absorbed: $|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}$ replaces $c^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}$, giving $(C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5}))\int|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma$ because $|C|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}c^{2})=C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})$ and one power of $\kappa_0$ cancels. (b) Rotate the integration variable so that $\beta_0=be_3$ with $b=|\beta_0|$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp e_1$ (rotation invariance of $\sigma$, [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); put $u=n_3$ and $\kappa_0=1-bu$. Expanding the numerator with $N=n\cdot\beta_0=bu$, $d=n\cdot\dot\beta_0$ and $|n-\beta_0|^{2}=1-2bu+b^{2}$ gives, exactly as in the recorded research computation, $$\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}=-(1-b^{2})(n\cdot a)^{2}+2\kappa_0 b\,a_\parallel(n\cdot a)+\kappa_0^{2}|a|^{2}.$$ Apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](b),(c) with $f(u)=(1-bu)^{-5}$ and $g(u)=(1-bu)^{-4}$: the azimuthal average turns $(n\cdot a)^2$ into $u^{2}a_\parallel^{2}+\tfrac12(1-u^{2})a_\perp^{2}$ and $n\cdot a$ into $ua_\parallel$, and $(1-bu)^{-3}$ weights the $|a|^{2}$ term. The resulting one-dimensional integrals are elementary: $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})(1-bu)^{-5}du=\tfrac{4}{3}(1-b^{2})^{-3}$ and $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-bu)^{-3}du=2(1-b^{2})^{-2}$, both verified by the displayed antiderivatives in $y=1-bu$ using the power derivative, chain rule and fundamental theorem ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Collecting terms gives $\int|\cdot|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma=(8\pi/3)[\gamma_0^{6}a_\parallel^{2}+\gamma_0^{4}a_\perp^{2}]= (8\pi/3)\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; multiplying by $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ produces (b). The four-acceleration identity is clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], where $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_w^{6}(w\cdot a)^{2}/c^{2}$ with $w=z'(s_0)=c\beta_0$ reads $\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; the $\beta_0=0$ case is the statement of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) The strongest immediate eventwise bounds are gamma0^4 P_L<=P_em<=gamma0^6 P_L, since |a|²-|beta0 cross a|² lies between (1-b²)|a|² and |a|². With b<=delta, gamma0>=1 and gamma0^6<=(1-delta²)^-3, they imply P_L<=P_em<=(1-delta²)^-3 P_L. A larger inverse factor in the UNIFORM lower bound is not justified by an upper bound on b (the rest event b0 disproves it). The rational identity (1-delta²)^-3-1=(3delta²-3delta^4+delta^6)/(1-delta²)^3<=3delta²/(1-delta²)^3 proves the unchanged difference estimate, including P_L0. (d) records that the definition is per unit emission time, that the near-field contribution vanishes after weighting by the uniform remainder and that no dynamics or empirical content is added. To make the finite angular integration fully explicit: the parallel averaged numerator is1-u²; the perpendicular one is(1-bu)²-(1-b²)(1-u²)/2. For b>0 the first transformed antiderivative is b^-3[(1-b²)y^-4/4-2y^-3/3+y^-2/2], y=1-bu, evaluated from1-b to1+b. At b0 direct angular moments give8pi|a|²/3; never evaluate a b^-3 antiderivative at b0. The angle-axis rotation preserves the existing sphere measure.

items.title: Self-force, runaways and finite-size regularizations are not supplied by this page
items.statement: Every cited conditional result retains its stated hypotheses. In particular, the point-source and causal-wave comparisons below assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) through their source suppliers; this qualification supplies no additional field or self-interaction model. Record, with no speculative content, the limits of the radiation model built on this page. (a) [Self-energy] For nonzero charge $q\ne0$, the truncated electrostatic field energy of the stationary idealized point charge diverges as the inner cutoff is removed ([[pthm-em-point-self-energy-divergence]]): the point source's own field carries infinite energy in this framework's idealization, and any finite-energy treatment of a point-like charge requires modifying the source or the field near the singularity, or an explicit cutoff, none of which is supplied here. The $q=0$ branch has zero field energy and no divergence. (b) [Undefined self-interaction] The framework's source model [[def-em-weak-sources]] pairs distributions against compact smooth tests and expressly excludes arbitrary products of distributions; the point charge's field is singular on the worldline while its own current is a distribution supported there, so the pairing of the charge's own field with its own current -- the object a systematic self-force would have to use -- is not defined by these postulates, no regularization is adopted, and no equation of motion for the charge is derived. (c) [What the emitted-power items do and do not give] [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] and [[pthm-em-lienard-emitted-power]] are prescribed-source statements: they compute the emitted power of a stipulated worldline at a stipulated emission event and determine no worldline evolution, no back-reaction and no coordinate-time rate; they are not a mechanical model. (d) [Deferred, not claimed] Extended-charge or finite-size regularizations of the self-field, the well-posedness of any self-force dynamics, runaway solutions and an electromagnetic derivation of rest mass are outside this page and are neither stated nor proved here. No experiment, measurement, statistical estimate or precision is reported or implied, and nothing in this remark is a refutation of any physical theory.

items.title: A smooth pointwise subluminal curve with no retarded root at an event
items.statement: Let $c>0$ and $a>0$, and define $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ by $z(s):=(\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[thm-of-square-roots]]). Then: (a) $z$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ and $|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$; nevertheless there is no constant $v_*<c$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for all $s$, because $|z'(s)|\to c$ as $s\to\pm\infty$; (b) at the event $(x,t)=(0,0)$ the retarded equation $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] has no solution in $\mathbb R$: the equation reads $-s=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$, whose right-hand side is at least $a/c>0$, and squaring both sides would give $c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}=c^{2}s^{2}$, i.e. $a^{2}=0$, contrary to $a>0$. Hence pointwise subluminality of a smooth curve does not by itself produce the retarded root, and the uniform bound $v_*<c$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]], or an explicit cone-intersection hypothesis, cannot be dropped; the supplier [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] indeed assumes such a uniform bound. (c) [Scope] This is a mathematical example about the prescribed curve and the root equation. The curve is future timelike pointwise ($|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s$) but not uniformly subluminal; it is not asserted to be the worldline of any physical charge, and no measurement is reported. The example contradicts no theorem: it exhibits a curve lying outside the hypotheses of the root lemma.
items.strategy: Direct verification. (a) $s\mapsto c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}$ is smooth, positive and bounded below by $a^{2}>0$, and $\sqrt\cdot$ is smooth on $(0,\infty)$; the chain rule and the derivative $\tfrac{d}{dt}\sqrt t=1/(2\sqrt t)$ give $z'(s)=(c^{2}s/\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$, whence $|z'(s)|=c^{2}|s|/\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}<c$ for every $s$ (at $s=0$ the speed is0; for $s\ne0$ it also equals $c/\sqrt{1+a^{2}/(c^{2}s^{2})}$) ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-square-monotone]], algebra), while $|z'(s)|\to c$ as $s\to\infty$; so no $v_*<c$ bounds $|z'|$ on all of $\mathbb R$. (b) For $x=0$, $t=0$ the root equation of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] is $-s=|z(s)|/c=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$. Since the right-hand side is positive, $s<0$, so both sides of $-s=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$ are positive and squaring is an equivalence: it gives $c^{2}s^{2}=c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}$, i.e. $a^{2}=0$, contradicting $a>0$; alternatively, the root lemma's existence proof requires the uniform Lipschitz bound $|z(s_2)-z(s_1)|\le v_*|s_2-s_1|$ with $v_*<c$, which fails here. (c) states the scope; no physical or empirical interpretation is attached.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the surface and finite-source branches. Adopt the electric-dipole radiation-law idealization whose leading far fields and angular flux are the dipole expressions of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], evaluated for the prescribed smooth waveform $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ with $\omega>0$ and $p_0
e0$. This is an explicit ideal radiation-law model, not an eternal compact-time source claimed to satisfy that theorem with $D=0$. Here $r>0$, $u\in\mathbb R$, $p_0\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ carries C m, $\omega$ carries s$^{-1}$, and $e_1,e_2,e_3$ are the standard orthonormal spatial basis. The waveform is an explicitly prescribed time-dependent dipole moment as defined in [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], not measured data; [[def-em-electric-moments]] supplies only the static moment convention. All exact quantities below refer to that ideal leading radiation law. Then: (a) [Fields] With $n=\sin	heta\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin	heta\sin\varphi\,e_2+\cos	heta\,e_3$, $	heta\in[0,\pi]$, $\varphi\in[0,2\pi]$, the ideal leading far fields are $$E_{\mathrm{lead}}(rn,u+r/c)=- rac{\mu_0\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)}{4\pi r}\,n	imes(n	imes e_3),\qquad B_{\mathrm{lead}}= rac{n	imes E_{\mathrm{lead}}}{c},$$ with $|n	imes(n	imes e_3)|=|\sin	heta|$, so the amplitude pattern is $\propto\sin	heta$ and vanishes on the dipole axis $	heta\in\{0,\pi\}$. (b) [Angular power density] The retarded-time angular power density of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] is $$ rac{dP}{d\sigma}(n,u)= rac{\mu_0|n	imes p''(u)|^{2}}{16\pi^{2}c}= rac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{16\pi^{2}c}\,\sin^{2}	heta,$$ the $\sin^{2}	heta$ pattern with zeros along $\pm e_3$ and maximum in the equatorial plane when $\cos(\omega u)
e0$; at times with $\cos(\omega u)=0$ the density vanishes in every direction; its integral over the sphere is $$\int_{S^2} rac{dP}{d\sigma}d\sigma= rac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c},$$ using $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}	heta\,d\sigma=8\pi/3$ from [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](a). (c) [Period average] The mean of the total power over one retarded-time period $u\in[0,2\pi/\omega]$ is $$ rac{\omega}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi/\omega} rac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c}\,du= rac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}}{12\pi c}.$$ (d) [Scope] The computation is the exact dipole law of the model; a finite prescribed source realizes it only within the absolute error bound of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] with its $D(u)$, and a physical antenna's feed, current distribution and material realization are additional source models not supplied here. The average in (c) is taken in the retarded-time variable, not in observation time; no measurement, radiation resistance, matching condition or effective area is reported, and no empirical claim is made. (e) [Actual compact-window realization] Choose a compact smooth time cutoff $\eta\equiv1$ near one selected period, a nonnegative $C^\infty$ bump $\sigma$ supported in $B_a$ with integral $1$, and $p_\eta(u)=\eta(u)p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$. Define $ho(y,u)=-p_\eta(u)\cdot
abla\sigma(y)$, $J(y,u)=p_\eta'(u)\sigma(y)$. These are smooth compact spacetime sources, satisfy continuity, carry zero total charge and have moment $p_\eta$. On the chosen period the moment equals the harmonic waveform, while the actual retarded field has the full $D(u)$, $\Gamma_E/r^{2}$ and $(\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c)/r^{2}$ errors of the dipole theorem. Its asymptotic total-power deviation from the ideal law is bounded by that theorem's explicit $R(u)$; its period-averaged deviation is bounded by the average of $|R(u)|$. The condition $V=p''$ is a sufficient ideal transverse-moment condition; it is not equivalent to $D=0$. No eternal nonzero harmonic moment is asserted for a compact-time source.
items.strategy: Direct substitution in [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. (a) $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ gives $p''(u)=-\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives|the scalar multiple rule]]), and clause (c) of the theorem gives $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times p'')/(4\pi r)$ with $B_{\mathrm{lead}}=n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}/c$ up to the stated errors; these are the ideal leading amplitudes; a finite-radius compact-source field still has its Gamma/r² remainder, even if a dipole-replacement error happens to vanish. The identity $n\times(n\times e_3)=n(n\cdot e_3)-e_3$ with $n\cdot e_3=\cos\theta$ and the Pythagorean identity give $|n\times(n\times e_3)|=|\sin\theta|$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]). (b) Clause (d) of the theorem gives the limit $\mu_0/(16\pi^{2}c)\int|n\times V|^{2}d\sigma$ with $V=p''$; substituting $p''$ and using $|n\times p''|^{2}=|p''|^{2}\sin^{2}\theta$ yields the displayed density. Its integral uses $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})du=2\pi\cdot(4/3)=8\pi/3$ by [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](a) with $f(u)=1-u^{2}$; multiplying $\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)/(16\pi^{2}c)$ by $8\pi/3$ gives $\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)/(6\pi c)$. (c) The average uses $\int_0^{2\pi/\omega}\cos^{2}(\omega u)du=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$: substitute $v=\omega u$ or exhibit the antiderivative $\tfrac{u}{2}+\tfrac{\sin(2\omega u)}{4\omega}$ and evaluate at the endpoints by the fundamental theorem ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]); multiplying the mean value of $\cos^{2}$ by the coefficient gives the displayed result. (d) states the scope; no measured or fitted quantity appears, and the period average is explicitly in retarded time. For (e), choose a nonnegative smooth compact cutoff positive on a ball, normalize by its strictly positive finite Lebesgue integral, and scale that unit-mass bump to have support inside B_a ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]]) and eta by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Continuity is rho_t=-p_eta' dot grad sigma and div J=p_eta' dot grad sigma. Integration by parts with zero boundary gives integral rho0 and integral y_i rho=p_eta_i integral sigma=p_eta_i. Therefore [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] constructs the actual fields; [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] gives their moment identities and complete finite-radius and flux errors, not an exact D0 premise for a time-varying harmonic current. Integrating the absolute error over one selected period gives the claimed average-error bound.
items.physical_scope: Deterministic model computation in the exact electric-dipole law for declared parameters: the $\sin^2\theta$ angular pattern and period-averaged power $\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}/(12\pi c)$ of a prescribed harmonic dipole moment, together with an actual compact-window source realization carrying the dipole theorem's explicit finite-radius and flux errors. Excluded: antenna feed, material and matching models, radiation resistance, measurements and every empirical statement.

items.title: Conditional radius loss of a prescribed slowly orbiting charge in a reduced quasistatic model
items.statement: When invoking the cited point-source emitted-power theorem as an established interpretation, retain its Countable Choice premise ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]). The reduced loss-rate formula in (H) below is independently adopted as a modelling hypothesis; the conditional finite-calculus orbit computation from (H) uses no choice. Adopt the following idealized, hypothetical setup of a prescribed slowly orbiting charge; it is a thought experiment with explicit premises, not a reported measurement. (H) Let $m>0$ be an externally supplied rest mass and $q\ne0$ a charge parameter ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]), let $\kappa>0$ carry J m, and let $J_t\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, $t_0\in J_t$, and $r:J_t\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$, with $r_0:=r(t_0)>0$. The reduced model assigns to each radius the circular-orbit values about a fixed laboratory centre ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]) for the attractive potential $V(r)=-\kappa/r$: the circular-orbit energy is $E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r)=-\kappa/(2r)$ and the circular orbit with speed $v$ satisfies $mv^{2}=\kappa/r$, with centripetal acceleration $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$. These are instantaneous circular reference values, not the exact kinematics of a curve with varying radius. To specify the intended validity window, choose dimensionless bounds $0<\delta_v,\delta_a<1$ and require $v(t)/c\le\delta_v$ and $T_{\rm orb}(t)|r'(t)|/r(t)\le\delta_a$, where $v(t):=\sqrt{\kappa/(mr(t))}$ and $T_{\rm orb}(t):=2\pi r(t)/v(t)$; the second ratio measures fractional radius change in one reference period. Independently adopt that the electromagnetic energy emitted per unit time is instantaneously taken to be the Larmor value $q^{2}a(t)^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] evaluated at the instantaneous centripetal acceleration, so that the adopted energy balance of the reduced model reads $$\frac{d}{dt}E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r(t))=-\frac{q^{2}a(t)^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}.$$ Then, with $A:=q^{2}\kappa/(3\pi\varepsilon_0m^{2}c^{3})>0$: (a) the reduced model implies $r'(t)=-A/r(t)^{2}$ for all $t$ where the model applies, and the circular orbit radius in the reduced model obeys $$r(t)^{3}=r_{0}^{3}-3A(t-t_{0})$$ on any interval containing $t_0$ on which $r>0$; (b) $r$ is strictly decreasing on $J_t$. The scalar balance ODE, considered without the validity-window inequalities, has the unique maximal positive continuation $\widehat r(t):=(r_0^3-3A(t-t_0))^{1/3}$ on $(-\infty,t_*)$, where $t_*:=t_0+r_0^3/(3A)$. It restricts to $r$ on $J_t$ and satisfies $\widehat r(t)\downarrow0$ as $t\uparrow t_*$; assigning zero at $t_*$ is only a continuous endpoint extension, not a positive-radius solution; (c) [Scope and qualifications] the deduction is conditional on (H). The low-speed premise $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\ll c^{2}$ necessarily fails as $r\to0$, so the model's own hypotheses break down near the collapse time and the computation is not a proof that a physical orbit reaches $r=0$; it is not a derivation of atomic lifetimes, not a coupled point-particle self-force calculation (that dynamics is not available in this framework), and it supplies no empirical evidence. The reduced-model finite-time collapse is retained as a mathematical property of (H), while all conclusions about nature remain conditional on (H) and on its regime of validity. No measurement, dataset, statistical model or uncertainty is introduced.
items.strategy: A complete conditional deduction from (H). (a) Differentiate $E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r)=-\kappa/(2r)$ along $r(t)$: the power rule gives $\tfrac{d}{dt}(-\kappa/(2r))=\kappa r'/(2r^{2})$ ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); the balance (H) reads $\kappa r'/(2r^{2})=-q^{2}a^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$; substituting $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$ and solving for $r'$ gives $r'=-q^{2}\kappa/(3\pi\varepsilon_0m^{2}c^{3}r^{2})=-A/r^{2}$. Multiplying by $3r^{2}$ gives $\tfrac{d}{dt}(r^{3})=-3A$, and the fundamental theorem applied on any interval where $r>0$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[def-interval]]) yields the displayed cubic; equivalently, differentiating the cubic reproduces the ODE, so the two are equivalent in the reduced model. (b) $r'=-A/r^{2}<0$ since $A>0$, so $r$ is strictly decreasing wherever the model applies; from the cubic, $r(t)^{3}\downarrow0$ as $t\uparrow t_{*}=t_{0}+r_{0}^{3}/(3A)$, and $r(t)^{3}<0$ beyond $t_{*}$ records the breakdown rather than a negative radius. (c) The scope clause records the failure of $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\ll c^{2}$ as $r\to0$, the absence of any coupled self-force dynamics in the framework (the point self-field is singular and its product with the current is undefined, as recorded by the scope remark on this page), and the absence of empirical content: this is a mapped, reduced model with a finite-time formal collapse, exactly as stated, and the conclusion is conditional on (H) throughout. The Larmor energy-loss expression is explicitly ADOPTED in(H) for the reduced slowly orbiting mechanical model, not obtained by pretending each laboratory orbit event is a rest event. The preceding Larmor theorem supplies the rest law and quantified general low-speed comparison; converting a prescribed emitted power into this mechanical balance remains the separate assumption(H). The ODE deduction itself uses only the stated scalar balance and finite calculus, and proves no self-force law.
items.physical_scope: Reduced quasistatic circular-orbit model with an adopted Larmor energy-balance premise (H): the radius ODE $r'=-A/r^{2}$, the cubic solution $r^{3}=r_{0}^{3}-3A(t-t_{0})$ and the formal finite-time collapse limit as a property of (H). Excluded: any claim that a physical orbit reaches the centre or an atom decays in finite time; coupled self-force dynamics; derivation of lifetimes; measurements, statistical models and every empirical claim.
